A man-in-the-middle (MITM) attack is when an attacker secretly positions themselves between two parties and intercepts their communication.
Conceptually, it breaks trust in the channel rather than necessarily breaking the app itself.
Common outcomes include eavesdropping, message tampering, credential theft, or session hijacking when integrity and authenticity checks are weak or absent.

Can I browse man pages by heading, including in nvim or LazyVim?

Short answer: man finds and formats a manual page, then hands the result to a pager. The macOS man program and its usual pager, less, do not expose the page's headings as a navigable hierarchy. Neovim's built-in man-page viewer does: open the page with :Man tmux, then press gO for a table of contents.
Can I browse man pages by heading, including in nvim or LazyVim?
Can I browse man pages by heading, including in nvim or LazyVim?

The installed /usr/bin/man accepts -P pager; MANPAGER overrides PAGER. Its default is less, whose navigation is text-based: search for an uppercase heading with /^COMMANDS$, then use n and N to move among matches. A broader search such as /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9 /_-]*$ finds many top-level headings. less does not parse those matches into an outline. Answer/Official from OpenBSD man(1) and less(1).

This machine currently sets MANPAGER to col -bx | bat --language=man --style=plain --paging=always. CLI/Tool/bat supplies highlighting and invokes a pager for scrolling, but it does not add heading-aware navigation.

In the man-page buffer, gO opens a location-list outline. Select an entry and press Enter to jump to it; q closes the outline or man window. On the installed tmux(1) page, Neovim finds the main headings plus many indented command and option entries, so the outline is more detailed than a list of top-level sections.
Can I browse man pages by heading, including in nvim or LazyVim?
Put the cursor on a reference such as printf(3) and press K or Ctrl-] to open that man page; Ctrl-T returns. Answer/Official from Neovim's man-page documentation and gO outline documentation.

For a one-off shell invocation using Neovim as the pager: MANPAGER='nvim +Man!' MANWIDTH=999 man tmux. MANWIDTH=999 reduces hard wrapping before Neovim receives the formatted page. To make this the default, export those variables in the shell configuration; that would replace the current bat-based MANPAGER pipeline.

The current LazyVim setup uses the nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim/Picker. <leader>sM opens its Man Pages picker, which searches for a page to open. After choosing tmux(1), press gO in the resulting man buffer to browse its internal outline. The picker chooses a manual page; Neovim's built-in gO provides the heading navigation. Answer/Official from LazyVim's Snacks picker mappings.
